questions.prompt: Match each part of a PLC to what it does.

pairs.right: Turns the plant's power into the low DC voltage the electronics need
Runs the program, over and over
Connects lights, valves and contactor coils
Holds the modules in numbered slots

questions.explanation: The processor decides; the input and output modules connect it to the machine; the power supply and the rack hold it all together.

questions.prompt: What is the main reason PLCs replaced relay panels?
options: The logic is a program: to change what the machine does, you edit the program, not the wiring
A PLC needs no wiring at all
A PLC can switch a motor's full current directly
Relay panels cannot use push buttons
questions.explanation: The buttons, sensors and contactors are still wired to the PLC, but only once. The logic between them is a program, which is quick to change and easy to watch running.

questions.prompt: Which of these are true of a **modular** PLC? Choose every one that is.
options: You choose the processor and add the input and output modules the machine needs
A failed module can be swapped without replacing the whole PLC
The power supply, processor and a set number of inputs and outputs are always in one box
Each module sits in a numbered slot
questions.explanation: Everything in one box describes a compact (fixed) PLC. A modular PLC is built up from separate modules in slots.

questions.prompt: You write a program on your laptop and copy it into the PLC. What is that called?
questions.explanation: Download is from the PC to the PLC; upload is from the PLC back to the PC.
